source.title: Don't Sweep your Learning Rate under the Rug: A Closer Look at Cross-modal Transfer of Pretrained Transformers
source.authors: Dan Rothermel; Margaret Li; Tim Rocktäschel; Jakob N. Foerster

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are supplied
record.tranche_reason: The study reports cross-modal transfer results and train/test gaps, but does not test any of the listed versions about memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture bias, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.gate_note: Reports train/test accuracy gaps and comparisons of pretrained, random, frozen, and unfrozen transformers. These results concern generalization but do not measure a behavior named by the listed versions; rows are recorded under versions ["none"]. Claims about Lu et al. are prior-work comparisons, not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate sensitivity of cross-modal transfer with pretrained, random, frozen and unfrozen transformers. None of its results tests V1–V8. Random initialization is not random-label memorization; changing transformer depth is not widening beyond interpolation; an Adam learning-rate sweep is not an optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: tuning learning rates overturns earlier claims favoring mostly frozen transformers, and full fine-tuning of pretrained transformers matches or exceeds training from scratch across the tested tasks. 'Best results' should allow ties: Table 1 does not show Unfrozen Pretrained numerically winning every task.
record.recipe_differences: Cross-modal transfer experiments using pretrained or random GPT2 variants, with a learning-rate sweep; no random-label memorization protocol or listed generalization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes absolute performance and the ordering between frozen and unfrozen variants across tasks; model capacity has little or no impact on MNIST and benefits some variants on CIFAR10 and CIFAR10-LRA.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports task-dependent train/test gaps across initialization and freezing settings. Frozen variants underfit MNIST and CIFAR10, while Frozen Pretrained has the largest ListOps gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Train/test gaps in cross-modal transformer transfer depend on task, initialization and which parameters are trained.

fits_no_version.finding: After learning-rate tuning, unfrozen variants outperform frozen variants on all four tasks. Unfrozen Pretrained matches training from scratch on ListOps and CIFAR10 and improves MNIST and CIFAR10-LRA performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate tuning can reverse conclusions about freezing pretrained transformers for cross-modal transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: The six-layer versus twelve-layer comparison shows task- and variant-dependent accuracy changes, with little or no effect on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing transformer depth has task-dependent benefits in cross-modal transfer.

record.code_released: https://github.com/kzl/universal-computation (referenced as the code released with Lu et al.; this paper's own code URL not stated)
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The supplied results concern four tasks, and the paper notes that some original tasks were not replicated. Table 3 reports train/test gaps at maximum gradient steps; it does not isolate the mechanisms named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out accuracy under random versus natural labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting from excessive dropout, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: T5 is inappropriate because the challenged claim concerns freezing in cross-modal transfer, outside V1–V8. The citation to Choi et al. motivates learning-rate tuning but supplies no own-result test of V4. Row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the numerical gaps themselves are reported. Table 3 uses final training steps, whereas Table 1 reports validation-selected checkpoints.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep past zero training error for one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures trained from scratch on images.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention and its effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
